transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-14
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Jenna (Redwood SE), Tom (Redwood CSM), Maya (Aster Proc), Liam (Aster Sec), Sofia (Aster Legal), Ben (Aster Eng)

Summary (auto): Align on MSA/DPA redlines and KMS clause; review SLAs and billing approval path; agree on concrete next steps and owners.

00:00 Samir (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you carving time out. quick agenda—walk MSA redlines, KMS clause ask from Aster, SLA levels we can commit to, and then billing and procurement gating. Jenna will cover technical options for Dedicated vs Private.
00:22 Maya (Aster Procurement): Thanks Samir. We're on a tight procurement timeline — finance wants sign-off by end of month if possible. primary blockers are KMS custody language and a clear SLA for availability and incident response.
00:38 Jenna (Redwood SE): Understood. We'll map options: hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private VPC. each has different key management tradeoffs. for hosted we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations, with envelope encryption; for private you keep full control.
00:55 Liam (Aster Sec): quick clarification — when you say KMS integration, is that cloud KMS or do you support HSM imports? we need to know if keys can be imported to HSM and whether rotation is in our control.
01:12 Jenna: we support both customer-managed cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure) with CMKs and we also have a private deployment option that can integrate with on-prem HSMs via PKCS#11. rotation cadence is configurable; we can agree on rotation windows in the SLA.
01:31 Sofia (Legal): from legal's side, the DPA currently has a standard clause about encryption "at rest" but we'd like explicit language that keys are under customer control and Redwood cannot access plaintext for private deployment. also need indemnity language around unauthorized disclosure.
01:49 Samir: totally — we can propose explicit language for private deployments. for hosted we typically offer envelope encryption with CMKs, and we can show audit logs. for the indemnity ask, we need to balance with our liability caps — can you flag what you're looking for so we can take it to legal?
02:07 Sofia: sure, we'll annotate. main ask: 1) customer keys for on-prem/private, 2) for hosted, clear auditability and key access control, 3) a narrow exception list for emergency access with customer notification.
02:25 Tom (Redwood CSM): I'll add our audit log artifact and sample attestation. we also have SOC2 and ISO documents that we can share in the portal. link to docs: https://redwood.example.com/security/docs (see "KMS & Key Custody" doc).
02:44 Ben (Eng): On the billing side, finance needs predictable cost buckets. what's the difference in unit economics if we do dedicated reserved capacity vs hosted pay-as-you-go?
03:01 Jenna: good question. high-level: hosted pay-as-you-go has higher per-token cost but no commitment; dedicated reserved capacity lowers unit cost but needs commit. we can model based on your traffic profile — if you send say 200M tokens/month, dedicated is usually 40-60% cheaper. i'll prepare a spreadsheet.
03:20 Maya: that's helpful — procurement needs a clear FY number for the approval chain. they also want to understand fallback behavior if capacity is constrained.
03:35 Samir: our routing supports fallback to compatible model variants or burst capacity. we can put an SLA for fallback time and explain throttling policies in the annex.
03:50 Liam: can SLA include incident response times for security incidents? e.g., initial acknowledgment within 1 hour and initial remediation steps within 4 hours?
04:06 Samir: ack. for enterprise Dedicated/Private customers we can commit to a 1-hour ack and a 4-hour initial remediation window for P1 security incidents — we just need this to be scoped in the contract (and tiered by support level).
04:18 Sofia: liability cap conversation — we need to escalate to our GC, but a carve-out for gross negligence is necessary. any chance Redwood can accept a higher cap in that case?
04:33 Samir: we usually have contract liability caps tied to annual fees, but we can discuss exceptions for gross negligence with legal. i'll include language options in the redline.
04:47 Ben: technical question — you mentioned prefix/KV cache and session tokens. will any customer data be persisted outside EU regions? Aster requires EU residency for PHI-like data.
05:04 Jenna: we support region pinning; for hosted we can pin to eu-west, and for private deployments all data remains in your VPC. we'll document data flows in the DPA annex.
05:21 Maya: great, procurement will want that data flow chart in the package.
05:33 Samir: noted. Sofia, can you call out which clause you want in the DPA about data residency and deletion timelines? that will speed reviews.
05:46 Sofia: yes, we'll annotate the DPA with a short list: deletion within 30 days of termination, EU-only processing for designated datasets, and export control exceptions.
06:03 Jenna: about SSO — we support SAML and OIDC, and can do SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC can be mapped to your internal roles. any constraints there?
06:18 Liam: SAML is mandatory for us. we also want SCIM for automated provisioning to avoid manual invite flows during onboarding.
06:27 Tom: we can deliver an onboarding checklist that includes SAML metadata exchange and SCIM mapping. average onboarding time for Dedicated is ~3 weeks once access is provided.
06:44 Maya: procurement will need that estimate in the packet. also they care about invoice timing — monthly vs quarterly billing and whether prepaid reserved capacity is possible.
06:56 Samir: finance options: monthly consumption billing for hosted; for dedicated we offer monthly or annual committed billing. we can do prepaid reserved credits for a year — that tends to get better unit pricing. I'll include the pricing tiers.
07:12 Ben: any penalties for over-commit or unused reserved capacity?
07:20 Jenna: we have burst credits and a flexible rollover option for some contracts, but heavy unused commitments are typically non-refundable. we can include a moderation clause in the commercial annex.
07:34 Sofia: will you be able to provide a redline of the MSA that highlights the KMS/HSM language and SLA values? that's what legal will look at first.
07:46 Samir: yes — i'll send a redlined MSA and a short explanation doc that maps each redline to rationale.
08:00 Maya: timeline recap: procurement wants sign-off by end of Jan. is that realistic if we get the redline this week?
08:12 Samir: if we get your annotated DPA and KMS policy this week and exchange the redline, we should be able to close procurement gate by end of month, assuming no major new asks.
08:26 Liam: note — one technical constraint: our HSM vendor uses a specific PKCS11 wrapper that had compatibility quirks in past. can we run a quick POC with a dev box?
08:41 Jenna: yes, we can spin a private deployment POC in a lab environment. it usually takes 5 business days to provision a test instance and validate PKCS11 integration.
09:00 Ben: if the POC proves messy, does Redwood offer professional services or will we need third-party integrators?
09:09 Tom: we have an integration services team and we can include a scope estimate. pro services would be a separate line item.
09:20 Sofia: another legal note — support SLAs around encryption key loss scenarios. what's Redwood's stance if keys are lost due to customer error?
09:34 Samir: for customer-managed keys, responsibility typically remains with the customer; we provide guidance and best practices. in private deployments we can assist with recovery tooling if you've escrowed keys with a protector service.
09:49 Sofia: ok will flag that for GC.
10:00 Maya: procurement will also ask for a short exhibit showing the escalation path — who signs off on credits, who approves emergency support.
10:12 Tom: i'll attach our escalation matrix and support tiers to the packet.
10:23 Ben: re pricing approvals — do you have a typical procurement checklist for finance approvals or a template PO we can attach to the contract?
10:36 Samir: yes we have a procurement packet: SOW template, PO template, and billing contact sheet. i'll drop that in the follow-up email.
10:47 Liam: competitor question — we're also talking to Anthropic and Bedrock for a multi-vendor approach. if we go multi-cloud, will Redwood provide routing controls and cost telemetry per model?
11:03 Jenna: we support smart routing and per-model telemetry. we can surface token costs per model and route by policy; that makes multi-vendor comparisons easier.
11:15 Maya: perfect. procurement will like the transparency.
11:25 Sofia: any export control considerations — does Redwood have anything flagged for restricted imports/exports?
11:36 Samir: we keep export control compliance in our compliance docs. i'll surface the relevant section — for EU-only processing there are no special export flags unless you're dealing with ITAR-level data.
11:50 Ben: circling back to SLAs — can we get explicit numbers in the MSA? e.g., uptime 99.95% for Dedicated, 99.5% for hosted, plus credits structure?
12:05 Samir: yes, we can propose those numbers. final credit mechanics will be in the SLA annex.
12:18 Sofia: and latency SLOs for realtime endpoints? our product is latency sensitive for some flows.
12:29 Jenna: we publish 95th percentile latency numbers per model and region in the perf annex; for Dedicated customers we can include narrower SLOs and monitoring hooks.
12:40 Maya: that will be part of procurement scoring.
12:49 Samir: ok quick recap before we wrap — action items: i'll send redlined MSA; Jenna will do cost/perf spreadsheet and POC provisioning notes; Liam will send KMS/HSM vendor details; Sofia will annotate DPA; Tom will supply onboarding + escalation docs. agreed?
13:07 All (various): yes / sounds good / thanks
13:18 Samir: great. i'll email the packet and schedule a 30-minute follow-up for next week to review the redline. any final blockers?
13:29 Maya: none from procurement now; timeline is tight but doable.
13:36 Sofia: we'll try to turn around the DPA comments within three business days.
13:43 Liam: i'll get the KMS briefs out by Tuesday.
13:50 Tom: i'll attach the SOC2 and the KMS attestation in the portal.
14:00 Samir: thanks everyone. end call.

Post-call notes:
- Shared artifacts referenced during call: procurement packet (link), MSA v3 redline draft (to be sent), KMS & key custody doc (portal), perf baseline template (to be attached).
- Tone: cooperative; procurement timeline tight; no show-stopping legal items flagged but indemnity/cap monies need GC review.

Transcript end.
